solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Provide funding for riverside function, we hear

indicators.note: what 'we hear' is only the spoken version, so the spelling may differ from the words supplied

blocks.note: a river's side is its bank
a function is a role, which is said the same as a roll

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to pay for a party held by the river, or so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riverside function' reads as a waterside party; split it into two words that together are said like the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bankroll a venture is to supply the money behind it, an informal synonym for financing.

clue.text: Best end to introduce spinner

indicators.note: to introduce something is to come just ahead of it, so one piece is placed before the next

blocks.note: the tip is the end of something
a spinning top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: Cricket advice: the ideal end from which to bring on the spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a cricket spin bowler, but here it is the child's toy that spins.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop is an informal adjective meaning excellent, of the highest quality.

clue.text: People watching a nude, ice dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places, so they come out in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, taken as written

explanation.surface: Spectators gawp at a naked figure skater on the rink.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the phrase, but the letters of 'a nude, ice' run together as one batch.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience is the group of spectators at a show or performance.

clue.text: River surrounded by support under dry conditions

definitions.note: a phrase describing a state; the answer is the adjective for that state

indicators.note: a thing surrounded by another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river
to aid is to support

explanation.surface: A river is propped up by help in a time of drought.
explanation.walkthrough: AID wraps round R to give A-R-ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid describes land or climate with very little rainfall, the state of being parched.

clue.text: Humour mostly upset scoundrel, a US politician

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: comedy is humour
a rat is a scoundrel or betrayer

explanation.surface: Mocking jokes have annoyed a rogue who sits in Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: Clip the last letter of COMEDY, turn COMED upside down to DEMOC, then add RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of one of America's two major political parties.

clue.text: Expression of hesitation over tirade as “rambling”

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means sitting above, so the first piece comes before the next

blocks.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A speaker's hesitant 'er' before a long tirade is dismissed as rambling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' sounds like a judgement on the rant, but it is the definition, in the sense of wandering.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means straying or wandering from the proper course, as a knight errant roams in search of adventure.

clue.text: Cooper’s first to put down the greatest boxer

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the name
to lay is to put down

explanation.surface: Henry Cooper, the British heavyweight, famously floored the young Cassius Clay in 1963.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassius Clay was Muhammad Ali's birth name; Ali called himself 'the greatest'. Cooper knocked him down in their 1963 London fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali, nicknamed The Greatest, boxed as Cassius Clay early in his career.

clue.text: R and A support item for a different sport

blocks.note: the two letters taken as written
a pier is a supporting pillar

explanation.surface: The R and A, golf's governing body at St Andrews, backs equipment for some other game.
explanation.walkthrough: The R&A runs golf; the 'different sport' is fencing, where a rapier is a type of sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender thrusting sword, equipment for fencing rather than golf.

clue.text: Wrong to restrict core of something remembered for all time

indicators.note: the core is the very centre, so only the middle letter is kept
to restrict is to hem in, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: morally wrong
the fifth of its nine letters

explanation.surface: Holding back the heart of something unforgettable would be wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: IMMORAL takes in the T at the centre of 'something' to give IMMOR-T-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone immortal lives forever, here in the sense of lasting fame that never fades.

clue.text: Without money, having to ditch new comedy performance

indicators.note: to ditch something is to throw it away, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: skint is British slang for broke
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A broke comic has to drop the fresh sketch from the act.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is everyday British slang for having no money; remove its N.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch, often parodying something.

clue.text: Argument against company name

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone objects to the name chosen for a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against company' looks like it belongs to the argument; the definition ends at 'against'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cons in 'pros and cons' are the points raised in opposition.

clue.text: Competition, true, developed item of IT

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: comp is British shorthand for a competition
taken as written

explanation.surface: A contest has genuinely produced a new piece of tech kit.
explanation.walkthrough: COMP, the short form of competition, is followed by the letters of TRUE rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer is the central piece of equipment in information technology.

clue.text: Discuss buy-out without first European to secure end of deal

indicators.note: without means lacking, and 'first' says which of two matching letters is the one removed
the end of a word is its last letter, so only that is kept
to secure is to hold fast, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: a takeover is a buy-out of a company
E is the abbreviation for European
the final letter

explanation.surface: Negotiators debate a company buy-out minus its first European partner to clinch the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The buy-out word has two Es, so 'first' matters: only the earlier one goes, and 'buy-out' is wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk over a matter is to consider it in conversation, a phrasal-verb equivalent.

clue.text: Time to imitate recording

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to ape is to imitate

explanation.surface: An impressionist decides it is time to copy a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the standard abbreviation for time, and to ape someone is to mimic them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape is a recording made on magnetic tape, such as an audio or video cassette.

clue.text: Favourite Disney film losing millions? Start to turn peevish

indicators.note: losing something means it is gone, so a letter drops out
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
Mulan is a Disney animated film
M is the abbreviation for millions
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A beloved Disney picture flops at the box office, and its makers start to sulk.
explanation.walkthrough: Mulan is Disney's 1998 animated film about a Chinese woman warrior; 'Start to turn' supplies a single letter at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulant describes childish bad temper, the sulky irritability that peevish also names.

clue.text: Tire following delay

blocks.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a lag is a delay

explanation.surface: A runner grows weary after a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like a link word, but it supplies F, as in 'pp. 5f'.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to lose energy or droop, the same as growing weary.

clue.text: Left for France, showing little sensitivity

blocks.note: first meaning: the French word for left
second meaning: socially awkward and tactless

explanation.surface: Someone departs for France, behaving rather tactlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a past tense of leave, but it is the direction, and 'for France' asks for the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: In English the borrowed word means awkward or lacking social grace, the clumsiness traditionally linked with left-handedness.

clue.text: Able to read line and repeat

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: A pupil is able to read a line aloud and say it again.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the usual abbreviation for line; iterate is a formal word for repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A literate person has learned reading and writing skills.

clue.text: British twice blocking government showing evidence of collapse

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, so one piece is lodged within the other

blocks.note: B for British, written two times
rule is government

explanation.surface: Two British parties obstruct an administration, a sign it is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Government' looks like the start of the definition, but it is wordplay: rule in the sense of governing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubble is the broken masonry left after a building falls down, physical proof of its fall.

clue.text: Nature reserve dispatching first rescue vessel

indicators.note: dispatching the first means sending away the opening letter

blocks.note: a national park is a nature reserve

explanation.surface: A wildlife reserve sends out its first rescue boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the P from PARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's ark is the boat that saved the animals from the Flood.

clue.text: Tube platform is packed everywhere to begin with

indicators.note: what each word begins with is its opening letter, so only those are kept

blocks.note: opening letter
opening letter
opening letter
opening letter

explanation.surface: A London Underground platform is crowded from end to end at the start of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' suggests the London Underground, but it is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe is a hollow cylinder for carrying liquid or gas, a synonym for tube.

clue.text: Public demonstration possibly skipping first bridge

indicators.note: skipping the first means passing over the opening letter

blocks.note: a protest march is one kind of public demonstration

explanation.surface: A protest march might avoid the first bridge on its route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' signals that a march is only one example of a demonstration; drop its M.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch is a curved span, and a bridge of the foot is called its arch.

clue.text: Striking book from the past

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
old things come from the past

explanation.surface: An impressive antique volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' sounds like hitting, but here it is an adjective meaning eye-catching.
explanation.definitionFit: A bold colour or design is vivid and eye-catching, which is what striking means.

clue.text: Find time to play new record?

blocks.note: a record is a vinyl disc
you put on another record once the current one has finished

explanation.surface: A DJ looks for the moment to spin a fresh record.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful phrase: it is time for a new record when the disc is over, read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to come upon or uncover it for the first time.

clue.text: Settlement evasive about extended cut

indicators.note: something cut has been shortened, so its last letter is removed
about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: coy means reluctant to give details
long means extended

explanation.surface: A legal settlement is vague on the matter of a lengthy reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settlement' suggests a legal deal, but it means a community of settlers; 'cut' trims a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony is a community of people settled in a new territory.

clue.text: Investigation here, with cars involved in crash

indicators.note: things involved in a crash are smashed and jumbled, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police are investigating at the scene where vehicles collided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crash' sets a road-accident scene; it signals that the letters of the two words get mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is systematic study aimed at establishing facts, a close synonym of investigation.
